\[
\begin{gathered}
M = M_{\text{XYZ}}^{-1} M_A^{-1}
\begin{bmatrix} \rho_t / \rho_s & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \gamma_t / \gamma_s & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \beta_t / \beta_s \end{bmatrix}
M_A\, M_{\text{XYZ}},
\quad
(\rho, \gamma, \beta) = M_A\, W,
\quad
\text{from } \text{A} \text{ to } \text{D65}
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(M_{\text{XYZ}}\): The linear sRGB to XYZ matrix
- \(M_A\): The cone response matrix of the method
- \(W_s, W_t\): The XYZ white points of the source and target lights
- \(\rho, \gamma, \beta\): The cone-like responses of a white

The color goes from linear sRGB to XYZ with M_XYZ, then to cone-like responses with M_A, the matrix of the method. There each response is scaled by the ratio of the target white W_t to the source white W_s, which is the von Kries idea. Then it goes back to XYZ and to linear sRGB. The white points are those of the CIE illuminants in ASTM E308-01, and the Bradford and von Kries matrices are those tabled by Lindbloom. XYZ scaling uses the identity for M_A. The whole chain is one 3 by 3 matrix, applied in linear light. The source white turns into the target white exactly.
